merged_from: The errored guard is applied only to `decision_flips`, but `_recall_false_accept` has no errored guard, and the tests never assert the errored pair's effect on recall/false-accept or on `report.passed`. An errored gold-block item (production shape `decision="dropped", label="block"`) is still scored as a recall miss, so the bar can still fail via criterion (c) — contradicting the change's stated 'attributes the event once instead of twice' contract. `test_errored_pair_is_not_a_decision_flip` uses exactly this shape yet asserts only `decision_flips`/`errored_pairs`/no-'flip'-failure, so the suite cannot detect this regression.

No test exercises an errored gold-SAFE pair, so the false-accept interaction with errored records is unexercised. Production errored records synthesize `decision="dropped"` (not 'block'), which currently does not inflate false-accept, but nothing pins that: a change to the errored decision vocabulary (e.g. to a blocking value) would silently start scoring runtime errors as false-accept regressions with no failing test.
